reasoning: The narration promises interactive exploration ('start exploring it', 'dive into each one interactively') but the tool shows only a static diagram. This creates a fundamental promise-reality gap that confuses students across all levels. Average confusion of 5/10 with Sam (struggling) at 8/10 indicates the current approach isn't working. Students expect to click, animate, and see data flow through the pipeline but can't. The tool cannot answer basic questions about what flows between stages or what 'interactive exploration' means.

strengths: Good transition from theory to practice
Emphasizes active learning over passive reading
Sets clear expectation for hands-on exploration
weaknesses: Uses undefined jargon ('conceptual scaffolding') that confuses struggling students
Promises interactivity that the tool doesn't provide
Doesn't define basic concepts like 'pipeline' for students who need scaffolding
Too abstract without concrete grounding before moving to the diagram

requirements.description: Animated data flow showing concrete objects (model weights, preference pairs, reward scores) moving through the pipeline stages with clear labels
requirements.reason: Students need to see what actually flows between stages rather than just arrows - resolves confusion about whether models are copied, frozen, or shared
requirements.studentNeed: Alex needs precision about model state management, Jordan needs to see the process in action

requirements.description: Clickable pipeline stages that expand to show detailed view with concrete examples and real numbers (e.g., R(x,y) = 0.73)
requirements.reason: Delivers on the promised 'interactive exploration' and lets students dive into each stage as narration promises
requirements.studentNeed: Jordan expects clickable exploration, needs to see actual reward values rather than abstract R(x,y)

requirements.description: Progressive disclosure mode that shows one stage at a time with simple before/after examples
requirements.reason: Reduces visual overwhelm and provides concrete examples before abstract pipeline view
requirements.studentNeed: Sam is overwhelmed by multiple diagrams and needs simple, sequential presentation

requirements.description: Toggle between 'simple view' (basic pipeline metaphor) and 'technical view' (detailed data flow)
requirements.reason: Allows struggling students to understand pipeline concept before seeing technical complexity
requirements.studentNeed: Sam needs to understand what a pipeline IS before seeing the technical implementation

requirements.description: Add clear visual indicators for which components are trained vs frozen at each stage
requirements.reason: Resolves ambiguity about model state management that confuses strong students
requirements.studentNeed: Alex needs clarity on whether SFT model is shared, copied, or frozen for PPO initialization and KL reference
